Answer: D
Reason: The combination of right-sided findings (pleural effusion, atelectasis/hypoplasia) and a prominent left second arc (enlarged pulmonary artery suggesting pulmonary hypertension) is characteristic of Scimitar syndrome (partial anomalous pulmonary venous return), where the anomalous vein drains to the IVC causing right lung hypoplasia and secondary pulmonary hypertension.
